title: Correlated usage ledger merge for cross-pool checkouts
creator: Mateo Rivera
description: Problem summary: When tenants with reserved capacity are rebalanced across GPU pools (cross-pool checkout / migration) we sometimes observe inconsistent quota accounting in the tenant usage ledgers. Symptoms include transient negative available_quota, duplicated token consumption events, or missing consumption after a checkout followed by a fast reset window (daily/monthly). Root causes appear to be a combination of: 1) concurrent merge of per-pool ephemeral ledgers without a deterministic merge order, 2) in-flight requests that were accounted locally and then re-applied post-migration, and 3) small replication lag between pool controllers and the central quota service which causes racey reset boundary handling. This ticket proposes an explicit correlated-merge algorithm and handoff protocol that makes cross-pool ledger merges idempotent, ordered, and observable.
context: Background: Reserved capacity uses per-pool ephemeral ledgers to minimize tail-latency token checks. On pool handoff (scheduled migration, preemption, or explicit checkout) we currently stream buffered usage events to the central ledger and mark the pool as drained. Corner cases when migrations happen right before a quota reset (midnight/monthly boundary) have led to reconciliation diffs and manual billing adjustments. Past fixes (soft-rollforward/epoch anchoring) reduced incidence but did not address deterministic ordering or merge-level idempotency, especially when multiple parallel migrations affect the same tenant.
proposed_solution: 1) Introduce a correlated-merge protocol: each pool emits a monotonic handoff-sequence token for the tenant (handoff_id + vector timestamp). The central ledger accepts a merge only when it can form a total order across handoff_ids for that tenant. 2) Apply a two-phase handoff: PREPARE (stream current ephemeral transactions with a snapshot version) and COMMIT (mark ephemeral ledger as drained after central ack). 3) Add an at-most-once de-duplication window using (tenant, request-id, handoff_id) keys in the central accumulator. 4) When a handoff spans a reset boundary, side-channel the snapshot reset-marker and merge it as a special transaction so the central state transitions resets deterministically. 5) Emit structured telemetry events (merge-start, merge-commit, merge-conflict) and expose an operator dashboard to replay/inspect merges.
acceptance_criteria: Central ledger reports no duplicated consumption events after simulated parallel checkouts (test harness)
End-to-end integration test that migrates a tenant across 3 pools during a daily reset boundary with no net change in billed tokens
New telemetry events appear in the billing observability dashboard and include handoff_id and vector_timestamp
Performance impact: p95 check path latency increase < 2ms with default batching
Rollback-safe: if commit fails, ephemeral pool continues to serve with backpressure and remains authoritative until manual intervention
implementation_notes: Add handoff_id generator to pool controller (UUID v7) and attach incremental local-seq numbers per tenant
Extend central ledger schema: last_accepted_handoff_id (string) and last_vector_ts (string) -- stored as strings to keep document schema flat

Write a merge worker that consumes PREPARE messages and attempts to build a total order using vector timestamps per tenant. Worker is idempotent and persists an acknowledgment record for each (tenant, handoff_id).
Create integration test harness that can fast-forward time to cross midnight/month boundaries and inject concurrency between PREPARE and COMMIT
Instrument requests with request-id in SDKs (fallback to generated id server-side) to enable de-duplication
Migration path: run worker in read-only analysis mode first (emit warnings) for two weeks before enabling commit path
Document new operator runbook for manual replay and conflict resolution stored in internal Confluence link
testing_plan: Unit tests for merge worker logic, property-based tests that assert commutativity of merges, end-to-end integration test with tenant migration through 3 simulated pools during reset boundary, and a staged rollout (canary on non-production reserved cluster) that runs in observation mode before commit-enabled rollout.
rollback_plan: If we detect increased reconciliation errors or customer-impacting double-billing in canary, flip central ledger to read-only merge mode and roll back pool controllers to previous wiring (ephemeral streaming to old aggregator). Use operator runbook to replay uncommitted handoffs and reconcile using historical telemetry. Automated alerts will open ENG incident ticket and mark affected tenants for manual audit.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Centralized ordering could become a bottleneck. Mitigation: shard ordering by tenant namespace and rate-limit large tenants into their own workers.
Risk: Vector timestamp skews under clock drift. Mitigation: use hybrid logical clocks (HLC) per pool controller to avoid reliance on perfectly synchronized clocks.
Risk: Long-running PREPAREs cause availability issues. Mitigation: set PREPARE timeouts and fallback to draining with temporary throttling, emit alerts for manual review.
Risk: Edge-case resets with fractional-day proration. Mitigation: merge reset as a dedicated transaction and run a deterministic ledger transition function documented in PRD.
